To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

companies contributing to the green-ing of consumption are those with products that have a high potential for environmental improvements, and those that are able to communicate environmental information to consumers in a way that is relevant to them.

consumer-oriented corporate strategies for greening consumption are visible in Thailand, particularly among larger companies, and that the dairy industry has only recently started to engage in this trend, whereas the appliance industry has a longer history of consumer-oriented CSR strategies.

companies contributing to the green-ing of consumption are those that offer green products and environmental information, story-lines, and images reflecting both general sustainability topics and consumer eco-lifestyles, such as those found in the Thai appliance industry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how companies can contribute to a greening of consumption, and how they can benefit from it.
the role of corporations in greening consumption, a subject that has received little attention in the academic literature, particularly with regard to low- and middleincome countries.
how the greening of consumerism is reflected in companies' strategies, products, and communication, as well as the underlying conditions and factors that influence the adoption of such strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the greening of Thai consumption is in its infancy.
consumer-oriented CSR is a growing phenomenon in Thailand, but its scope and depth vary considerably between industries and companies.
greening consumption has become a relevant part of corporate strategies in the dairy and appliance industry in Thailand, but that there is a lot of room for improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dairy and appliance companies have started to green consumption, but their strategies and performances are not yet fully developed and integrated into business operations.
the dairy industry is in a nascent phase of green consumerism and appliance manufacturers are in the process of building their green image.

the dairy and appliance companies have been able to develop a range of green products, but that the dairy companies still need to develop more sophisticated strategies for communicating with consumers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

companies in Thailand have started adopting CSR strategies aimed at reducing their environmental footprints and are increasingly using environmental information, narratives, and images to communicate their environmental performance to consumers.
the environmental performance of companies varies considerably, even within the same industry.
the dairy industry has a long way to go to catch up with the appliance industry, which has been more proactive in developing green products, information, and narratives.
